svg.aria-label: pheasant role-split fleet at maximum configuration: sources and SDK connectors feed one indexer that is the sole commit authority, which hands bytes to N gRPC preparation workers and drains a NATS JetStream index queue; it is the only writer of PostgreSQL and the state volume, which N graph-free API replicas and one graph service read; agents, operators and a Synapse router consume the API; model endpoints, the observation, evaluation, tuning and readiness planes, and three separate service tokens sit alongside.
svg.text: pheasant — the role-split fleet at maximum configuration
deploy/compose/docker-compose.scale.yml + fleet.yaml · postgres · NATS JetStream · gRPC workers · LanceDB · every plane enabled

g.text: api · s3 · memory (frontmatter Markdown, one file per record)
artifact id file:{source}:{relpath}:branch={b} is a contract
sources[].type resolves through entry points — no dispatch code
third-party plugins run at connector.runtime: sandboxed
wasmtime guest · fuel metering · linear-memory cap
a guest declaring an unwired import fails to load at all
watcher: 20 000 paths · 250 ms debounce · 1 s batch window
scheduler beat 900 s · memory, IdP and reclamation upkeep
drains PHEASANT_INDEX · holds sync_lock and source_leases
sha256 unchanged → skipped before the bytes are ever read
SOLE COMMIT AUTHORITY — graph, vectors and FTS are one stream
a second indexer is elected hot standby, never throughput
remote preparation is an optimization: no arrangement of
worker failures may change what a sync produces
extract 7 doc formats · chunk · taxonomy · caption
gRPC round-robin · circuit breaker · deadline propagation
failover to another worker, then to local preparation
holds exactly one secret: the index-worker token
refuses a DSN, model key, graph token or source list
api.enabled: false is enforced — 404 outside the probes
generation id = XOR fold of row digests, O(changed) commit
a commit costs what the change costs, not what the graph is
internal graph API, behind its own token
reload announced on core NATS, per kb
30 s poll is the backstop, not the path
SqlGraph is the serving read surface:
it holds nothing, so it cannot go stale
hybrid retrieval, fused by RRF: text BM25 + vector (LanceDB) + graph arm
one over-fetch — ranking.filter_overfetch governs ACL, section, memory, criteria
services/ layer: one implementation, two transports, identical refusal text
memory policy · steering · validity at query time · acl_enforced: true
assistant: agentic workflow, 2 rounds, graph expand depth 2, citations verified
MCP streamable HTTP · bundled React UI · OpenAPI · Prometheus /metrics
32 concurrent → 429 + Retry-After · 20 s SIGTERM drain off the event loop
/ready publishes loaded beside published generation — staleness is detectable
the tool surface is public API:
bundled UI, baked into the image
bearer token at the front door · /internal/* is exempt structurally
the only sanctioned network calls at sync time
.transcript.txt sidecar always wins over the model
assistant gpt · 24 context chunks · evidence graded
Each keeps a deterministic offline stub, so the suite
stays network-free — and no LLM call ever enters the
indexing decision path. Determinism is a product
PLANES · each off by default, all on here
request path appends to a bounded ring only
serve --role logger drains PHEASANT_LOGS → rows → Parquet
rows, never files: never chunked, never searchable
session-digest-v1 writes; three further rules propose
six cohorts · paired ablations B0–B6 · typed proof
unknown is weight zero; silence is never a negative
gates evaluated before aggregation, never averaged away
__evaluation__ lease, never sync_lock · progress is a row
stage attribution: which step lost the document
400 re-fusion trials cost no retrieval · 24 re-query
a winner must confirm on a holdout it never saw
one fleet-scoped bundle; tune apply is a separate act
capability contract derived from live symbols, not written
corpus_denylist enforced at every door, in security/
verdict is tri-state — INCOMPLETE is not PASS
serve refuses to start when the graph and worker tokens name
one variable or resolve to one value. A worker is the least
trusted tier and holds the third by necessity.
